headline: Arete Group expands employee wellbeing focus through UMatter programme
summary: Arete Group has expanded its employee wellbeing initiatives by introducing the UMatter programme in partnership with mental health platform MindPeers. The initiative combines confidential counselling, early intervention resources, and leadership advocacy to normalize mental health conversations in the workplace. By framing wellbeing as a core business priority rather than a basic benefit, the company aims to foster a supportive work culture and reduce stigma.

headline: Engineers make up 42% of Vedanta workforce as group focuses on industrial skills
summary: Engineers now comprise 42% of Vedanta Group's workforce as the conglomerate expands its focus on both core industrial skills and emerging disciplines like AI, data science, and automation. The company recruits top talent from elite institutions to optimize operations across its mining, metals, oil and gas, and power businesses. Through internal mobility and structured training, Vedanta aims to build a flexible workforce equipped to handle modern digital transformation and sustainability goals.

headline: Wells Fargo fires employees over mouse jiggler use to simulate work activity
summary: Wells Fargo discharged over a dozen employees in 2024 after an internal review revealed they used 'mouse jigglers' to simulate keyboard activity and feign work presence. The incident highlights the growing adoption of digital monitoring tools by employers managing remote and hybrid workforces. Ultimately, the case underscores the limitations of using activity metrics rather than output-based productivity measures.

headline: Meta suspends employee data programme after 1,800 workers oppose computer monitoring
summary: Meta has suspended its internal Model Capability Initiative, a programme designed to track employee computer usage to train AI models on routine tasks. The suspension followed opposition from over 1,800 workers who raised concerns regarding privacy risks, internal data exposure, and potential job automation. Meta announced that any future iterations of the data-collection effort will require explicit employee opt-in.

headline: Rich countries use ChatGPT 36 times more than poor ones. Job exposure explains only part of the gap
summary: According to a World Bank report, high-income countries adopt ChatGPT at 36 times the rate of low-income nations, a disparity driven less by job exposure and more by underlying organizational readiness. Factors such as digital infrastructure, structured management, and prior cloud technology adoption heavily dictate a firm's ability to effectively extract value from AI. Consequently, while basic chatbot usage is common globally, sophisticated business integration remains concentrated in economically advanced markets.

headline: HR Perspectives by Rajita Singh: “Giving internal employees opportunities requires the same kind of thinking as hiring externally”
summary: Kyndryl HR leader Rajita Singh emphasizes that internal talent mobility requires the same strategic rigor and intentional skill assessment as external hiring. Instead of tracking simple training completion metrics, organizations must focus on building adaptable workforce capabilities that directly address evolving client needs. Consequently, modern HR leaders must tightly align workforce decisions with commercial strategy, revenue, and competitive advantage.

headline: IBM elevates Harish Bharti to CTO, Asia Pacific, IBM Consulting
summary: IBM Consulting has appointed Harish Bharti as its new Chief Technology Officer for the Asia Pacific region. A long-time IBM veteran who joined the firm in 2002, Bharti previously served as CTO for core systems modernisation and a distinguished engineer. In his new role, he will focus on driving enterprise transformation and scaling production-ready agentic AI across the region.

headline: Has Oracle laid off 2000 in India?
summary: Oracle has reportedly cut an estimated 2,000 to 2,500 jobs in India as part of an ongoing organizational restructuring. The layoffs reflect the company's strategic shift away from legacy software products toward cloud computing and artificial intelligence investments. Affected employees received abrupt termination notices despite Oracle's continued expansion of its regional data center infrastructure.

headline: Insurance not liable for employer’s penalty
summary: The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh ruled that insurance companies are not liable for interest or penalties resulting from an employer's delay in paying statutory workers' compensation. While the insurer must cover the baseline compensation agreed upon in the policy, default charges caused by late payments fall strictly on the employer. This decision clarifies that standard insurance policies cover statutory employee compensation but do not shield employers from default-related penalties.

headline: AirBaltic in talks with unions over workforce changes amid Chapter 11 restructuring
summary: Latvian carrier AirBaltic is negotiating with labor unions over potential job cuts and revised employment terms following its voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing in the U.S. The airline aims to reduce capacity and adjust its wet-lease operations to restructure debt while maintaining regular flight operations.

headline: India Post employee bodies back transformation into citizen-centric service network
summary: Representatives of India Post employee organizations have backed the agency's ongoing transformation into a citizen-centric service network providing expanded financial, digital, and public services across the country. During a meeting with Union Minister Jitendra Singh, employee leaders also raised key workplace concerns, including pension issues and organizational recognition. The government stated that employee matters requiring further review will be considered through standard administrative processes.

headline: Flipkart creates 2.5 lakh employment opportunities for festive season
summary: Flipkart plans to create over 2.5 lakh direct and indirect job opportunities across India for the 2026 festive season to meet rising demand in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets. Approximately 60% of these seasonal roles will focus on last-mile delivery, supported by the addition of more than 900 new delivery hubs. The expansion also emphasizes workforce diversity, reserving nearly 75,000 roles for first-time entrants while boosting participation among women and persons with disabilities.

headline: Reliance MET City names Manish Jaiswal CEO to drive next phase of growth
summary: Reliance MET City, a subsidiary of Reliance Industries, has appointed Manish Jaiswal as its new Chief Executive Officer to lead its next phase of growth. Jaiswal, who previously served as CEO at Eldeco Group and Tribeca Developers, will oversee overall strategy and business expansion across industrial, residential, and commercial sectors in the National Capital Region. In his new role, he will focus on attracting investments, strengthening strategic partnerships, and scaling the integrated urban hub.

headline: BoomerangHR secures $12.7M to build AI platform for boomerang hiring
summary: AI-powered offboarding and alumni management platform BoomerangHR raised $12.7 million in a seed round led by Kalos Ventures and Album Ventures. The company automates offboarding workflows to help businesses transform former employees into active networks for rehiring, referrals, and ongoing engagement. Industry leaders highlighted the platform's ability to create long-term value by maintaining strong relationships with departing talent.

headline: Rivaah by Tanishq brings many stories to one wedding
summary: Tanishq's wedding brand, Rivaah, has launched a new campaign titled 'One Wedding. Many Stories.' to highlight how modern brides craft their entire wedding experience beyond just jewelry. Conceptualized by ad agency TBWA\Lintas, the campaign integrates elements of destination, film, and photography, featuring creative collaborations with photographer Joseph Radhik and filmmaker Shoojit Sircar.

headline: BabyOrgano’s latest campaign sparks conversation on modern co-parenting
summary: Ayurvedic kids' wellness brand BabyOrgano has launched its first brand film, focusing on modern Indian co-parenting and shared childcare responsibilities. Developed in partnership with creative agency Team Pumpkin, the campaign depicts a father taking on daily parenting duties as the mother returns to work post-maternity leave. The initiative aims to spark realistic conversations around balancing parenting roles while subtly featuring the brand's wellness products.

headline: Max Cement launches Mil Kar Banate Hai campaign featuring Suniel Shetty
summary: Max Cement has launched its new regional brand campaign, "Mil Kar Banate Hai," featuring actor Suniel Shetty across all seven states of Northeast India. The multi-channel initiative highlights collective effort and community building to strengthen the brand's local market positioning. Produced by Ketchup Studios, the 360-degree strategy targets consumers, masons, and dealers through localized content and multi-language outreach.

headline: Badri Beriwal joins Bennett Coleman as director, brands, products and portfolio strategy
summary: Badri Beriwal has been appointed as the Director of Brands, Products, and Portfolio Strategy at Bennett Coleman & Co. Ltd. He brings extensive retail and marketing leadership experience from his previous role as Chief Strategy and Business Development Officer at Bata India, where he expanded the store network past 2,000 locations. Prior to Bata, Beriwal held executive positions at Britannia Industries, Stanley Black & Decker, and Veeba.

headline: Confessions of a Type-A planner in a 60-minute quick fashion world
summary: The quick fashion sector has rapidly expanded into a $13.5 billion market, driven by increasing consumer demand for apparel delivery within 60 minutes. Emerging D2C startups like Slikk and Snitch, alongside legacy e-commerce platforms like Myntra and Reliance's Ajio, are deploying ultra-fast services to capitalize on impulse shopping and immediate fashion needs. This trend underscores a broader shift toward instant gratification in quick commerce across major Indian metro cities.
